headline: After a man dies in police custody, residents in a Missouri town demand answers
summary: The death of Lloyd Gilmore, a Black man who died in police custody after seeking help at the Sikeston, Missouri police station, has sparked concerns about racial bias and excessive force among local Black residents. Despite national protests against police brutality in 2020, public attention to the issue has waned, with reduced funding for racial equity programs and less politically charged research topics. The city of Sikeston faces continued tension due to historical racial violence, with some residents calling for transparency and accountability from their police department.

headline: Border residents wanted crossings reined in. Now Paxton and Talarico face voters wary of deportations
summary: Texas Senate candidates Ken Paxton (R) and James Talarico (D) campaigned in border cities, reflecting the state's political focus on immigration issues ahead of the election.

headline: Texas faith leaders condemn ICE-related deaths, demand end to “terror campaign” against migrants
summary: Faith leaders, including Bishop Sue Briner of the Southwestern Texas Synod of ELCA, protested against ICE activities at the Texas Capitol on July 22, 2026.

headline: Higher education agency prepares to cut 3% of spending as ordered by Texas leaders
summary: Texas's budget projects a $4.6 billion deficit for FY 2026, primarily due to increased spending on public education and health care, and decreasing revenue from oil and gas production.

headline: Texas’ longstanding “Robin Hood” school finance system will face a new legal challenge
summary: Midland ISD's administration building was damaged on Oct. 7, 2025.

headline: Cornyn votes for Trump diplomatic nominees after securing funds for global HIV/AIDS initiative
summary: Sen. John Cornyn introduced a bill aiming to combat opioid abuse by improving data sharing between states and incentivizing treatment programs. This legislation could impact public health by enhancing surveillance of prescription drug misuse, potentially informing prevention strategies and treatment resources allocation across Texas and other states.

headline: Democrats press ICE on oversight, say 1 officer referred for discipline over use of force
summary: Since Trump's inauguration, one ICE officer has been referred for disciplinary action over use of force incidents. Concerns about ICE tactics have arisen following two shootings during arrests and a history of violent behavior by officers involved. Democrats question ICE's training methods and oversight processes, while Republicans appreciate ICE briefing members on their practices.

headline: Typo in House bill stifles $15 million meant to protect Mississippians from storms
summary: A typographical error in a Mississippi state budget appropriations bill left the Strengthen Mississippi Homes Program, intended to enhance residential resilience against natural disasters, underfunded by $15 million due to an incorrect bill reference. The error was not corrected before Governor Tate Reeves signed the legislation, impacting the program's initial $15 million allocation and limiting eligible participants to coastal counties with reduced funding of $2 million.

headline: UMMC to take over Greenwood Leflore Hospital Aug. 1
summary: After years of financial struggles and near closure, Greenwood Leflore Hospital will be taken over by University of Mississippi Medical Center (UMMC) on Aug. 1, ensuring continued healthcare services for the community. This transfer aims to stabilize the hospital's operations and may improve public health access in the area.

headline: Kendall Qualls wants to cut taxes and spending and roll back trans rights
summary: Kendall Qualls, a Republican gubernatorial candidate in Minnesota, plans significant budget cuts if elected. He proposes a $9 billion rebate for Minnesotans by reducing taxes and regulations, aiming to cut 12% across all departments. Despite endorsements and grassroots support, Qualls faces an uphill battle in the polls against competitors Lisa Demuth and Mike Lindell. The state's budget surplus is not explicitly mentioned but would likely decrease if his proposed rebate and cuts are implemented.

headline: Fifty for 150: Colorado state troops sent to Cripple Creek miners’ strike in 1894
summary: In 1894, Colorado miners struck for eight-hour workdays. Mine owners enlisted deputies and militia, leading to violence. Governor Waite intervened, threatening militia against mine owners' private army, ultimately enforcing an eight-hour day agreement.

headline: Colorado health officials still unable to investigate tuberculosis case at ICE detention facility
summary: Colorado health officials can't investigate a tuberculosis case at an Aurora ICE detention center due to GEO Group's lack of cooperation. This has raised concerns about immigration detainees' health and safety, as high temperatures in the facility were also reported. The incident has drawn attention from Colorado lawmakers, with Rep. Jason Crow stating that ICE is "out of control."

headline: Va. hospitals predict $31B reduction in state’s Medicaid funding if proposed CMS rule passes
summary: The proposed CMS rule could reduce Medicaid payments to healthcare facilities by $31 billion over a decade in Virginia, potentially impacting essential services like emergency care. Public health could be affected as reduced funding might limit access to preventive care and increase uninsured patient visits to ERs.

headline: Virginia Beach doctor pushes hospitals to establish protocols for dealing with Parkinson’s patients
summary: Parkinson's patients face challenges in receiving timely medications during hospitalizations due to standard medication round schedules. This issue can lead to complications such as falls and infections. The Parkinson's Foundation is working with hospitals nationwide to improve care, including allowing patient self-administration where possible. Despite efforts, progress has been slow, particularly in Virginia healthcare systems.

headline: State pours $21M into removal of aging, leaking petroleum tanks
summary: Indiana's proactive underground tank closure program has spent $21 million since 2023, reimbursing owners for half of decommissioning costs. Despite this, hundreds of old tanks remain statewide, posing potential environmental risks and financial burdens on local governments. The program has unused funds of $59 million, with an annual allotment of $20 million from the Excess Liability Trust Fund, which is funded by a one-penny-per-gallon inspection fee on motor vehicle fuels.

headline: Maryland cyclosporiasis cases spike, part of a national surge in intestinal illness cases
summary: As of July 20th, Maryland has seen a surge in cyclosporiasis cases, totaling 110 and contributing to the nationwide figure of over 4,173. The CDC is investigating multiple clusters, including one linked to Taylor Farms iceberg lettuce from Mexico. Public health officials advise thorough washing of all fresh produce and avoiding recalled lettuce during this outbreak.

headline: Deportation hearing for Salah Sarsour focuses on Israeli detention
summary: A federal immigration judge is reviewing whether Salah Sarsour, a Palestinian-American community leader arrested by ICE, should be deported. The hearing focuses on whether his past actions in Israel, including alleged involvement in protests and support for Palestinian rights, warrant his removal from the U.S. Despite living in the U.S. since 1993 with no criminal record, Sarsour faces possible deportation due to accusations stemming from his time under Israeli military occupation.

headline: Polls show Hong leading with almost half of voters undecided
summary: A Marquette Law School poll shows Rep. Francesca Hong leading Democratic gubernatorial rivals but trailing presumptive GOP nominee Tom Tiffany. Internal polls from opponents also show Hong leading. Polls suggest race is close, with significant undecided voters and potential for change due to recent candidate entry/exit.

headline: A specter of justice in Pennsylvania
summary: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled that life without parole for felony murder is unconstitutional under state law. This decision offers hope to hundreds incarcerated under this doctrine, but final implementation depends on the legislature's actions.

headline: State Police gets funding boost for cadet classes in new spending plan
summary: Pennsylvania's new budget allocates $16.2 million for state trooper training, aiming to fulfill Gov. Josh Shapiro's campaign promise of adding 2,000 troopers during his first term. The budget also includes a $4.5 million increase for information technology and radio systems. Funding for municipal police programs remained flat. This budget prioritizes public safety and law enforcement resources across the commonwealth.

headline: ICE withdraws appeal of Pa. environmental directives tied to warehouse purchases
summary: ICE has abandoned plans to convert two Pennsylvania warehouses into detention centers, following local infrastructure concerns and public opposition.

headline: ACLU sues Penn State Health over canceled gender-affirming care procedure
summary: Penn State Health canceled a gender-affirming surgery for EJ Stiles less than 24 hours before it was scheduled due to Catholic doctrine violations. ACLU filed a lawsuit arguing this violates Pennsylvania's anti-discrimination laws and constitutional rights, potentially impacting healthcare equality policies.

headline: ACLU of Montana settles with feds after trying to deport foreign MSU students.
summary: ACLU of Montana settles lawsuit with U.S. government, securing reinstatement of student visas for two international students at Montana State University who were initially threatened with deportation due to policy changes by the Trump Administration in 2025. The settlement ensures students' legal status and allows them to continue their education without fear of penalty.

headline: ICE detains Providence man facing deportation to country he has never known
summary: ICE detained Cambodian refugee Chansareth Hong, who lived in Rhode Island since infancy, for potential deportation to Cambodia despite being primary caregiver for autistic son and elderly mother. Governor McKee urged ICE not to detain him; local leaders intervened but could not prevent transfer to Wyatt Detention Facility. Activists protested, demanding his release and criticizing ICE's enforcement.

headline: Cyclosporiasis outbreak surges to over 4,173 confirmed cases
summary: Over 4,000 cases of cyclosporiasis, a parasitic infection causing severe intestinal issues, have been reported across 41 states, more than doubling since last week. The CDC estimates over 7,000 unreported cases, with no deaths but over 300 hospitalizations. Taylor Farms' shredded iceberg lettuce from Mexico is linked to at least 1,644 cases. Tracking cases and sources is challenging due to the complex parasitic genome, straining public health resources.

headline: Is it safe to eat lettuce? Upper Valley experts answer key questions on cyclosporiasis outbreak
summary: The Vermont Department of Health reports no cases linked to a national cyclosporiasis outbreak, but has seen infections within typical range. A California-based distributor recalled all iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico between June 29 and July 16 due to potential contamination. The recall is ongoing despite FDA walking back claims that a sample tested positive for the parasite. Local produce suppliers have seen increased sales as consumers prefer locally sourced products amidst national outbreaks. Public health officials advise thorough washing of all fresh produce, proper food handling, and hand hygiene to prevent cyclosporiasis infections.

headline: Brattleboro weighs a municipal tax hike to aid the local hospital’s endangered birthing center
summary: The closure of Brattleboro Memorial Hospital's birthing center due to financial struggles threatens public health access for Windham and Windsor counties. Medical groups urge Gov. Scott to increase Medicaid obstetric reimbursement rates, while Brattleboro considers a municipal tax hike to aid the center.

headline: Vermont Conversation: ‘I’m sorry that this isn’t what we promised.’ Immigration attorney Jill Martin Diaz on fear and hope in Vermont’s immigrant community
summary: Immigration enforcement under Trump intensifies, with ICE detaining over 10,000 people and killing two men within a week. Vermont's immigrant communities face constant fear despite Trump's claims of targeting only convicted criminals. VAAP, led by Jill Martin Diaz, supports immigrants but warns of eroding rights and protections. Haitians in Vermont may lose TPS, making them vulnerable to ICE detention and deportation.

headline: Nebraska budget hole grows to over $1 billion, with 5 months before next legislative session
summary: Nebraska faces dual budget deficits totaling over $1 billion by mid-2029. The current biennium (through 2027) has a projected deficit of $208 million, and the next one ($864 million). Lawmakers are expected to address these shortfalls in the 2027 session. Governor Pillen has initiated a voluntary 5% spending reduction across state agencies to mitigate budget cuts.

headline: WA agency director out as Ferguson installs an interim leader
summary: Gov. Bob Ferguson appointed Employment Security Department Commissioner Cami Feek as interim director of the Department of Enterprise Services following Matt Jones' resignation, effective July 9. No reason for Jones' leave was provided. This change may impact state facilities management but does not directly relate to protests or civil unrest.

headline: New Hampshire universities embark on $8M effort to understand rise in tick-borne illnesses
summary: New Hampshire receives $8M NSF grant for collaborative study on ticks' habitat and disease spread impacts, aiming to protect human and wildlife health.

headline: A state Senate primary could bring major changes to CT education
summary: The article discusses three Democratic candidates challenging incumbent Sen. Doug McCrory in Connecticut's 2nd Senate District, each prioritizing education funding, special needs support, and reducing segregation. They differ on approaches to school choice programs, but agree on equitable funding for all schools.

headline: Livingston County enters ICE cooperation agreement; sheriff says it ‘doesn’t change anything’
summary: Livingston County Sheriff's Office signs a 287(g) agreement with ICE to detain and deport undocumented immigrants already held on charges, aiming for a DOJ grant. This is the 10th-most populous county in Michigan, connecting major cities like Detroit and Ann Arbor where ICE has notable presence. Immigrant rights advocates criticize the decision due to concerns over racial profiling and harm to community-police relations.

headline: Beshear reverses 4% Kentucky Medicaid provider cuts
summary: Kentucky's budget surplus of $476 million, primarily due to an unanticipated corporate income tax payment, allowed Gov. Andy Beshear to cancel planned 4% Medicaid reimbursement cuts for providers and fund senior meal programs and Michelle P. Waiver slots through FY2023. However, Beshear warned not to rely on this funding source annually and urged the legislature to reopen the budget in January to ensure adequate funding for next fiscal year.

headline: New education commissioner is an ‘outstanding choice,’ Erika Donalds says
summary: Henry Mack was appointed Florida's new education commissioner, recommended by Gov. Ron DeSantis and praised by school-choice advocate Erika Donalds. Mack, an innovator with experience across various educational roles, replaces interim commissioner Paul Burns. His appointment aligns with Gov. DeSantis' vision for Florida schools, aiming to maintain the state's national leadership in education.

outlet: News From The States - Fair. Fearless. Free.
headline: US Senate Dems press Mullin to ensure all immigration agents have body cameras
summary: 38 Senate Democrats urge Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin to deploy body cameras for all federal immigration officers following fatal shootings of immigrants in Texas and Maine. They demand investigations into these incidents, highlighting a lack of prioritization by DHS despite ample funding for such equipment since 2021.

headline: Oklahoma records 170 ‘explosive diarrhea’ cyclosporiasis cases as spike continues
summary: Oklahoma has seen a surge in cyclosporiasis cases, with 170 confirmed and 12 hospitalizations. The CDC reported over 4,000 nationwide cases. A lettuce recall was initially announced but later deemed a false positive. Public health officials advise thorough washing of produce and cooking to kill parasites.
